card.summary: The ROTOR Act aims to improve aviation safety by expanding aircraft tracking and communication rules, tightening exceptions for government aircraft, and increasing oversight and coordination between the Federal Aviation Administration and military agencies.
card.title: ROTOR Act

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Rotorcraft Operations Transparency and Oversight Reform Act (ROTOR Act) addresses aviation safety by requiring aircraft to use ADS-B In equipment, narrowing exceptions for sensitive government missions regarding ADS-B Out equipment, repealing certain military helicopter exemptions, mandating various audits and safety reviews, and establishing information-sharing agreements between the FAA and military departments.

affected_groups.effect: Must equip affected aircraft with ADS-B In technology by December 31, 2031, following performance standards and alternative low-cost compliance options for aircraft under 12,500 pounds.
Face stricter definitions and reporting requirements for sensitive government mission exceptions to ADS-B Out transmission mandates, including quarterly reporting.
affected_groups.group: Federal, State, Local, and Tribal Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Must issue new rules for ADS-B In equipment, establish a coordination office, conduct extensive airport safety reviews, update air traffic controller training, and revise agreements with other agencies.

Lose previous exemptions for military helicopters in the Washington, D.C. area, face audits by the Army Inspector General regarding coordination and equipment use, and participate in safety information-sharing MOUs with the FAA.
affected_groups.group: Department of Defense and Military Branches

key_provisions: Requires aircraft (other than unmanned aircraft) required to be equipped with ADS-B Out to also be equipped and operating with ADS-B In equipment no later than December 31, 2031.

Narrowly construes 'sensitive government mission' exceptions for ADS-B Out requirements, excluding routine, non-classified, or proficiency flights, and flights of officials below Cabinet or Chairman rank.
Repeals a 2025 law exempting certain military helicopters from ADS-B Out requirements in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan area.
Requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review ADS-B Out exceptions, and the DOT Inspector General to conduct annual audits of FAA oversight.
Directs the FAA to establish an 'Office of FAA-DOD Coordination' and conduct safety reviews of flight operations around Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport and other Class B, C, and D airports.
Mandates that the FAA enter into Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with military departments and the Coast Guard for aviation safety information sharing.
missing_information: Exact financial costs or appropriations associated with retrofitting aircraft fleets and conducting mandated audits and reviews are not stated in the source text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Rotorcraft Operations Transparency and Oversight Reform Act (ROTOR Act) addresses aviation safety by requiring aircraft to use ADS-B In equipment, narrowing exceptions for sensitive government missions regarding ADS-B Out equipment, repealing certain military helicopter exemptions, mandating various audits and safety reviews, and establishing information-sharing agreements between the FAA and military departments.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping update to federal aviation safety laws regarding tracking technology, interagency airspace coordination, and military-civilian flight oversight. It affects all civil and military aircraft operators required to use tracking technology, commercial airports, and federal oversight bodies.
